title: A callable operation
intro: A tool is an operation exposed to the model through a documented interface. The application executes requested calls and returns their results.
takeaway: Tool descriptions guide selection. Execution, authorization and error handling belong in application code.

beats.text: The model needs incident information. A search tool exposes one operation.
The model requests that operation. The application receives a structured call.
The application executes the search. The model does not run it directly.
Return the result through the application. The model uses it as evidence.

title: Make inputs explicit
intro: A search needs a service, time range and result limit. Explicit input fields let the application reject invalid calls instead of guessing.
takeaway: Shape validation catches missing or invalid fields. It does not establish authorization or guarantee the query is useful.

beats.text: Search needs a service and time range. These are explicit input fields.
A call omits the end time. Validation finds the missing field.
Reject the invalid call before execution. Return an actionable input error.
A corrected call can reach the tool. Validate it before running the search.

title: Return usable evidence
intro: Useful results identify records and the scope searched. An incident summary should retain IDs and its searched interval so the answer can be checked.
takeaway: A valid output shape does not prove source completeness or correctness. Expose enough provenance to evaluate the result.

beats.text: The search finds incident records. A bare success flag is not enough.
Return IDs and short summaries. Include the interval that was searched.
The model can cite those records. Its answer has inspectable support.
Keep claims within the returned scope. Two found records are not all history.

title: Empty versus failed
intro: An empty completed search and a backend timeout are different outcomes. They must not share an ambiguous empty-list response.
takeaway: An MCP tool execution error uses its error signaling. A transport timeout may produce no tool result at all; preserve that failure too.

beats.text: A completed search finds no matches. That is an empty successful result.
Return success and an empty list. This supports no matches in that scope.
Now consider a backend timeout. That search did not establish no matches.
The model must preserve the uncertainty. It cannot claim there were no incidents.

title: Expose more pages
intro: A result limit bounds response size. If more matches exist, return a continuation cursor and make partial coverage explicit.
takeaway: A page is not the complete result set. Follow the cursor when the task requires more coverage and the budget permits.

beats.text: The search is limited to one page. More matches may remain.
Return the page and a continuation cursor. The caller can see that this is partial.
The model requests the following page. It reuses the cursor and query scope.
Page 2 returns without a next cursor. This query is complete; stop paging.
